These compounds all share a common target, NCI-H2171, suggesting a potential mechanistic link between Zeylanol and the disease state associated with NCI-H2171. The evidence points to a pathway where Zeylanol may modulate the activity of the T-type calcium channel subunit alpha-1I, potentially influencing cellular signaling processes that are relevant to NCI-H2171. The presence of multiple structurally diverse compounds targeting the same target implies that the interaction may be mediated through a common mechanism, possibly involving the modulation of calcium influx or other ionotropic receptor functions. The integrated evidence supports a plausible mechanistic relationship, though further validation through in vitro or in vivo studies is necessary to confirm the specific mode of action and therapeutic relevance.
